task_2.title: Drop Python 3.6 support, raise minimum to Python 3.7
task_2.description: Python 3.6 reached end-of-life on 2021-12-23 and is no longer supported by pytest as of version 7.1.0. All Python 3.6-specific compatibility code paths, polyfills, and version-conditional branches have been removed. The minimum supported Python version is now 3.7. Users running pytest on Python 3.6 will no longer be able to use this version.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that pytest 7.1.0 no longer supports Python 3.6 and that the minimum required Python version is 3.7. Ensure that all internal compatibility shims for Python 3.6 are removed, the library uses standard library APIs available since Python 3.7 unconditionally, and the assertion rewriting subsystem assumes the Python 3.7+ pyc bytecode format exclusively.

expectation.grounded: The nullcontext polyfill previously provided in _pytest.compat for Python 3.6 is removed; contextlib.nullcontext from the standard library is used directly. The AssertionRewritingHook no longer checks for spec.origin == 'namespace' (a Python 3.6-specific origin value) and unconditionally writes and reads the PEP 552 4-byte flags field in pyc headers (16-byte header format). The LoggingPlugin.set_log_path method uses logging.StreamHandler.setStream() unconditionally without a Python 3.6 fallback that manually acquires, flushes, and swaps the stream. LogCaptureHandler and _LiveLoggingStreamHandler inherit from a properly generic-typed logging.StreamHandler alias. The _windowsconsoleio_workaround function (formerly _py36_windowsconsoleio_workaround) retains its Windows console handling behavior. The subprocess.run call in LsofFdLeakChecker uses the text parameter instead of universal_newlines.
expectation.conceptual: The library raises its minimum Python version to 3.7 and removes all Python 3.6 compatibility code. Standard library facilities available since Python 3.7 (such as contextlib.nullcontext and StreamHandler.setStream) are used unconditionally. The assertion rewriting system assumes the modern pyc bytecode header format. All existing user-facing behavior for Python 3.7+ users remains unchanged.

constraints.grounded: All functionality that previously worked on Python 3.7 and above must continue to work identically. The assertion rewrite pyc format must remain compliant with PEP 552 for Python 3.7+. The log file handler stream-switching behavior must remain equivalent to the previous setStream() path. The Windows console IO workaround must remain functional on supported Python versions. The module-level __getattr__ deprecation warning for Instance must continue to be emitted.
constraints.conceptual: No regressions may be introduced for users on Python 3.7 or later. All test collection ordering, log capture, log file handling, assertion rewriting, and Windows console workaround behaviors must remain identical for supported Python versions. The removal of Python 3.6 support must not alter any observable behavior for users on Python 3.7+.

behavior: The library no longer installs or runs on Python 3.6; attempting to use it on Python 3.6 is unsupported.
contextlib.nullcontext is imported directly from the standard library instead of from a _pytest.compat polyfill.
The assertion rewriting hook no longer treats spec.origin == 'namespace' as a namespace package indicator; it only checks for spec.origin is None.
Pyc file writing unconditionally includes the 4-byte PEP 552 flags field, producing a 16-byte header.
Pyc file reading unconditionally expects a 16-byte header and validates the PEP 552 flags field at bytes 4-8.
LoggingPlugin.set_log_path uses StreamHandler.setStream() directly without a manual acquire/flush/swap fallback.
LogCaptureHandler and _LiveLoggingStreamHandler use a generic-typed StreamHandler base class alias for improved type checking.
The Windows console IO workaround function is renamed from _py36_windowsconsoleio_workaround to _windowsconsoleio_workaround.
LsofFdLeakChecker uses the text=True parameter instead of the legacy universal_newlines=True alias in subprocess.run.
The module-level __getattr__ in _pytest.python for the Instance deprecation warning no longer carries a caveat comment about Python 3.6 incompatibility.
acceptance_criteria: When pytest 7.1.0 is used on Python 3.7 or later, all existing test collection, execution, logging, and assertion rewriting functionality works identically to version 7.0.1.
When assertion rewriting writes a pyc file, the file contains a 16-byte header including the 4-byte PEP 552 flags field.
When assertion rewriting reads a pyc file, it expects exactly 16 bytes for the header and validates the flags at bytes 4-8 are zero.
When the assertion rewriting hook encounters a namespace package with spec.origin set to None, it correctly skips rewriting.
When LoggingPlugin.set_log_path is called, the log file handler's stream is replaced using StreamHandler.setStream() and the old stream is closed.
When log capture is active, LogCaptureHandler correctly captures log records to a StringIO stream.
When live logging is enabled, _LiveLoggingStreamHandler functions correctly as a logging StreamHandler.
When running on Windows with fd capture mode, the _windowsconsoleio_workaround is applied to stdout.
When the deprecated pytest.Instance is accessed, a deprecation warning is emitted via module-level __getattr__.
When contextlib.nullcontext is needed internally, it is imported from the standard library without any polyfill layer.

task_1.title: Remove features deprecated in pytest 6.x series
task_1.description: Pytest 7.1.0 completes the deprecation cycle by removing several public APIs and features that were deprecated in the 6.x series and converted to errors in 7.0. The removed features include the pytest._fillfuncargs function, the pytest_warning_captured hook, the deprecated -k expression syntaxes (-expr and expr:), the pytest.collect compatibility shim module, and the PytestRemovedIn7Warning warning class. Users relying on any of these deprecated APIs must migrate to their documented replacements.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement:
Ensure that all features deprecated during the pytest 6.x series and scheduled for removal in 7.0 are fully removed from the public API in version 7.1.0. Specifically:
- Ensure that pytest._fillfuncargs is no longer accessible as a public API.
- Ensure that the pytest_warning_captured hook is no longer defined or invoked.
- Ensure that the -k option no longer accepts the deprecated '-expr' (dash prefix) or 'expr:' (colon suffix) syntaxes.
- Ensure that the pytest.collect compatibility module is no longer available.
- Ensure that the PytestRemovedIn7Warning warning class is no longer exported or defined.

expectation.grounded: Calling or importing pytest._fillfuncargs must raise an AttributeError rather than emitting a deprecation warning. The pytest_warning_captured hook specification must not exist in the hook spec, and warning recording must only invoke pytest_warning_recorded. The deselect_by_keyword function must not perform dash-prefix or colon-suffix transformations on -k expressions; invalid expressions should raise UsageError. Importing from pytest.collect must raise a ModuleNotFoundError. The PytestRemovedIn7Warning class must not be importable from pytest or _pytest.warning_types. The associated deprecation constants FILLFUNCARGS, PYTEST_COLLECT_MODULE, MINUS_K_DASH, MINUS_K_COLON, and WARNING_CAPTURED_HOOK must no longer be defined in the deprecated module. The catch_warnings_for_item context manager must not install an error filter for PytestRemovedIn7Warning.
expectation.conceptual: All APIs and behaviors that were marked as deprecated in the 6.x release series are completely removed. Attempting to use any removed API produces an import error or attribute error rather than a deprecation warning. The warning infrastructure only uses the modern pytest_warning_recorded hook. The -k flag only accepts the current expression syntax. The pytest.collect compatibility shim no longer exists. No trace of the removed-in-7 deprecation warning class remains in the public interface.

constraints.grounded: The pytest_warning_recorded hook must continue to function exactly as before, receiving all warning messages during config, collect, and runtest phases. Existing valid -k expressions (boolean expressions using 'not', 'and', 'or') must continue to work unchanged. All items currently importable from the top-level pytest namespace (except the five removed names) must remain importable. The PytestRemovedIn8Warning class and its associated deprecation infrastructure must remain intact and unaffected. The YIELD_FIXTURE deprecation warning and WARNING_CMDLINE_PREPARSE_HOOK warning must remain defined and functional.
constraints.conceptual: The removal must only affect deprecated APIs; all non-deprecated functionality must remain fully operational. The modern replacements for each removed feature must continue working correctly. The deprecation infrastructure for the next release cycle (removed-in-8 warnings) must be preserved. Test selection, warning recording, and fixture resolution must all continue to function through their current non-deprecated interfaces.

behavior: pytest._fillfuncargs is removed from the public API; importing or calling it raises AttributeError
The internal _fillfuncargs, fillfixtures, and _fill_fixtures_impl helper functions are removed from the fixtures module
The pytest_warning_captured hook specification is removed from hookspec; plugins implementing it no longer receive calls
Warning capture during config initialization and test execution only invokes pytest_warning_recorded, not pytest_warning_captured
The -k option no longer converts '-expr' to 'not expr'; passing '-expr' is treated as a literal expression and may fail
The -k option no longer strips trailing colons or supports the 'expr:' select-until syntax
The pytest.collect module (FakeCollectModule shim) is deleted; importing pytest.collect raises ModuleNotFoundError
The PytestRemovedIn7Warning class is removed from _pytest.warning_types and from the pytest namespace
The automatic error filter for PytestRemovedIn7Warning is removed from catch_warnings_for_item
Deprecation constants FILLFUNCARGS, PYTEST_COLLECT_MODULE, MINUS_K_DASH, MINUS_K_COLON, and WARNING_CAPTURED_HOOK are removed from the deprecated module
acceptance_criteria: When a user attempts to call pytest._fillfuncargs(), an AttributeError is raised instead of a deprecation warning
When a plugin implements the pytest_warning_captured hook, it receives no calls during test execution because the hook specification no longer exists
When warnings are captured during config or test execution, only the pytest_warning_recorded hook is invoked
When a user runs pytest with -k '-foobar', the expression is not silently converted to 'not foobar' and instead is treated as a raw expression
When a user runs pytest with -k 'foobar:', the trailing colon is not stripped and the select-until behavior does not activate
When a user attempts to import from pytest.collect (e.g., pytest.collect.Module), a ModuleNotFoundError is raised
When a user attempts to reference pytest.PytestRemovedIn7Warning, an AttributeError is raised
When PytestRemovedIn8Warning-level deprecations are triggered, they continue to function normally and are not affected by these removals
When valid -k expressions using 'not', 'and', 'or' keywords are used, test selection works correctly as before

task_3.title: Fix assertion output verbosity levels showing incorrect detail
task_3.description: The verbose flag (-v) was paradoxically showing less information than default output for certain data types (non-sequence, non-set, non-dict), because a verbose-specific code path replaced the richer assertion introspection with a simplistic repr-based diff. Additionally, the quiet flag (-q) was incorrectly showing full sequence diffs instead of the expected truncated output, due to a faulty boolean check on negative verbosity values. Both issues are corrected so that verbosity levels now monotonically increase output detail.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that using the -v (verbose) flag during test runs never produces less informative failure output than the default (no flag) output for any data type. Ensure that using the -q (quiet) flag does not produce full sequence diffs that should only appear at higher verbosity levels. Specifically: (1) For assertion failures involving non-sequence, non-set, non-dict types, -v must retain the detailed assertion introspection (e.g., 'where N = len(...)') rather than replacing it with a bare repr diff. (2) For sequence comparison diffs, -q must show the same truncated hint as default verbosity, not the full expanded diff.

expectation.grounded: When _compare_eq_any processes assertion failures for types that are not sequences, sets, or dicts, verbose > 0 must not override the default assertion explanation with a less-informative repr-only diff. The _compare_eq_verbose helper and its invocation in the verbose > 0 branch should be removed so that the standard explanation pipeline applies regardless of verbosity for these types. In _compare_eq_iterable, the guard condition must use 'verbose <= 0' (not 'not verbose') so that both verbose=0 and verbose=-1 (quiet mode) produce the truncated 'Use -v to get more diff' hint rather than falling through to the full difflib output. The hint message should read 'Use -v to get more diff'.
expectation.conceptual: Assertion failure output detail must increase monotonically with verbosity level. The verbose flag must always show at least as much useful information as the default output. The quiet flag must never show more detail than the default output. For non-collection types, verbose mode must preserve the rich assertion introspection rather than substituting a simplified representation. For iterable comparisons, quiet mode must show a truncated hint directing the user to use -v, not the full diff.

constraints.grounded: Existing behavior for sequence, set, and dict comparisons under _compare_eq_sequence, _compare_eq_set, and _compare_eq_dict must remain unchanged. The running_on_ci() override in _compare_eq_iterable must continue to bypass truncation regardless of verbosity. The _compare_eq_iterable function must still produce full diffs when verbose > 0 or when running on CI. No changes to the public pytest API surface or command-line flag semantics.
constraints.conceptual: Collection-type-specific comparison logic (sequences, sets, dicts) must not regress. CI environments must continue to receive full diff output regardless of verbosity settings. The fix must not alter the meaning or behavior of any pytest command-line flags. Only the output formatting for the identified edge cases should change.

behavior: For non-sequence, non-set, non-dict types: assertion failures at verbose > 0 now show the same rich introspection output as verbose=0 (e.g., 'where 2 = len([...])') instead of a bare +repr/-repr diff.
For iterable comparisons at verbose=-1 (quiet mode): output now shows the truncated hint 'Use -v to get more diff' instead of producing the full difflib-based diff.
For iterable comparisons at verbose=0 (default): behavior is unchanged; the truncated hint is still shown.
For iterable comparisons at verbose > 0: behavior is unchanged; the full diff is still shown.
The truncation hint message is updated from 'Use -v to get the full diff' to 'Use -v to get more diff'.
acceptance_criteria: When a test asserts on a non-collection type (e.g., assert len(list_of_dicts) == 1) and is run with -v, the failure output should include the detailed 'where N = len([...])' introspection line, not just a numeric +/- diff.
When a test comparing sequences fails and is run with -q (quiet), the output should show the hint 'Use -v to get more diff' rather than the full expanded diff.
When a test comparing sequences fails and is run with default verbosity (no flags), the output should show the hint 'Use -v to get more diff'.
When a test comparing sequences fails and is run with -v, the output should show the full expanded diff.
When running on CI (running_on_ci() returns True), full diffs for iterable comparisons are shown regardless of verbosity level.
Assertion output for set, dict, and sequence-specific comparisons (via _compare_eq_set, _compare_eq_dict, _compare_eq_sequence) remains unchanged at all verbosity levels.

task_4.title: Skip specialized assert formatting for dataclasses/attrs with custom __eq__
task_4.description: When a dataclass or attrs class overrides the default __eq__ method (e.g., to perform numpy array comparison), pytest's specialized assertion introspection for class instances would crash or produce confusing internal error messages instead of a clean assertion failure. This change detects whether the __eq__ on a dataclass or attrs instance is the auto-generated default, and if not, bypasses the field-by-field comparison formatting, falling back to the standard assertion representation.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that when a dataclass or attrs class defines a custom __eq__ method, pytest assertion introspection does not attempt specialized field-by-field comparison formatting. Previously, this would trigger internal errors (e.g., ValueError from numpy arrays) or produce misleading 'faulty __repr__' messages instead of a straightforward assertion failure.

expectation.grounded: The _compare_eq_cls function must call has_default_eq on the left operand before performing field-by-field comparison. has_default_eq inspects __eq__.__code__.co_filename to determine whether the __eq__ was auto-generated: for attrs classes it checks for the substring 'attrs generated eq' in the code filename; for dataclasses it checks that the code filename equals '<string>'. If has_default_eq returns False (indicating a custom __eq__), _compare_eq_cls must return an empty list, causing pytest to fall back to the default assertion representation. If __eq__ lacks a __code__ attribute (e.g., built-in types), has_default_eq returns True, preserving existing behavior.
expectation.conceptual: When two instances of a dataclass or attrs class are compared in an assert statement, pytest should only produce detailed field-by-field diff output if the class uses its framework-generated default equality method. If the class provides a custom __eq__ override, pytest should fall back to its standard assertion output without attempting to introspect individual fields, thereby avoiding crashes or misleading error messages from non-standard equality logic.

constraints.grounded: Dataclasses and attrs classes that do NOT override __eq__ must continue to receive the existing specialized field-by-field assertion formatting with no change in behavior. Classes that are neither dataclasses nor attrs must be unaffected. The has_default_eq function must gracefully handle objects whose __eq__ lacks a __code__ attribute by returning True, ensuring no regressions for built-in types or C-extension types. The isattrs check must be applied before the dataclass filename check to ensure correct detection for attrs classes.
constraints.conceptual: Existing assertion formatting behavior for standard dataclasses, standard attrs classes, and all non-class comparisons must be fully preserved. The fix must only suppress specialized formatting when a custom __eq__ override is positively detected, never producing false positives that would remove useful diff output from classes using default equality.

behavior: A new has_default_eq utility function is introduced that inspects the __eq__ method's code metadata to determine whether it was auto-generated by the dataclass or attrs framework.
For attrs classes, has_default_eq checks whether the __eq__.__code__.co_filename contains the marker string indicating attrs-generated equality.
For dataclasses, has_default_eq checks whether the __eq__.__code__.co_filename equals the conventional '<string>' value used by the dataclass module's code generation.
If __eq__ has no __code__ attribute (e.g., built-in types), has_default_eq returns True to preserve existing comparison behavior.
The _compare_eq_cls function now calls has_default_eq before performing field-by-field comparison; if the result is False, it immediately returns an empty list.
When specialized formatting is skipped, pytest falls back to its standard assertion message showing the repr of both operands without field-level drill-down.
acceptance_criteria: When a dataclass with a custom __eq__ (e.g., one using numpy array comparison) fails an equality assertion, pytest should display the standard assertion error without field-by-field introspection and without any internal ValueError or 'faulty __repr__' messages.
When an attrs class with a custom __eq__ fails an equality assertion, pytest should similarly skip specialized formatting and display the standard assertion error cleanly.
When a dataclass using the default auto-generated __eq__ fails an equality assertion, pytest should continue to display the specialized field-by-field diff output exactly as before.
When an attrs class using the default auto-generated __eq__ fails an equality assertion, pytest should continue to display the specialized field-by-field diff output exactly as before.
When comparing non-class objects (dicts, lists, strings, etc.) in assertions, behavior should be completely unchanged.
When a class has a __eq__ without a __code__ attribute (e.g., C-extension or built-in type), the specialized formatting path should remain available and no errors should occur.

task_5.title: Show full skip/xfail reasons at high verbosity (-vv)
task_5.description: Previously, skip and xfail reasons displayed during test runs were always truncated to fit the terminal width, even when the user requested high verbosity with -vv. This made it impossible to read full skip reasons for tests with longer explanation strings. The update conditionally bypasses the truncation logic when verbosity is 2 or higher, so that skip and xfail reasons are displayed in full.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that when the user passes -vv (verbosity level 2 or higher), skip and xfail reasons are displayed in full without being truncated to fit the terminal width. At lower verbosity levels, reasons should continue to be trimmed to the available terminal width as before.

expectation.grounded: When config.option.verbose >= 2 and a test is skipped or marked as xfail, the TerminalReporter should write the full reason string (formatted as ' ({reason})') without passing it through _format_trimmed. When config.option.verbose < 2, the reason should still be trimmed via _format_trimmed using the available terminal width (fullwidth minus current line width minus progress indicator width). In both cases, if the reason is empty or the formatted result is None, nothing should be written.
expectation.conceptual: At high verbosity (-vv or above), pytest should display the complete skip and xfail reason text in the terminal output so users can read the full explanation. At normal or single-verbose levels, reasons should remain truncated to fit the terminal line width. Empty reasons should never produce output regardless of verbosity.

constraints.grounded: The truncation behavior via _format_trimmed must be preserved when verbose < 2. The guard against writing when reason is falsy or formatted_reason is None must remain. The _get_raw_skip_reason function must still be used to extract the reason. Progress information display (_write_progress_information_filling_space) must not be affected.
constraints.conceptual: Default (non-verbose and single-verbose) truncation behavior must not regress. The change must only affect the display formatting of reasons, not the extraction of reason text, progress indicators, or any other terminal output. Tests that are neither skipped nor xfail should be completely unaffected.

behavior: When -vv (or higher) is passed and a test is skipped, the full skip reason is displayed without truncation in the terminal output.
When -vv (or higher) is passed and a test has an xfail marker (wasxfail), the full xfail reason is displayed without truncation.
When verbosity is below 2 (no flag, -v), skip and xfail reasons are still truncated to fit within the available terminal width, preserving the existing behavior.
If the skip/xfail reason is empty, no reason text is written regardless of verbosity level.
The progress percentage indicator (e.g., [100%]) display is unaffected by this change.
acceptance_criteria: When a test is skipped with a long reason and -vv is passed, the full reason text appears in the output without trailing ellipsis or truncation.
When a test is skipped with a long reason and -v (single verbose) is passed, the reason text is truncated to fit the terminal width, matching the prior behavior.
When a test is skipped with a long reason and no verbosity flag is passed, the reason text is truncated to fit the terminal width, matching the prior behavior.
When a test has an xfail reason and -vv is passed, the full xfail reason appears without truncation.
When a test is skipped with an empty reason, no reason parenthetical is written regardless of verbosity level.
Given multiple skipped tests with varying reason lengths and -vv, all reasons are shown in full without any being cut off.

task_6.title: Enhanced ResourceWarning output with tracemalloc allocation tracebacks
task_6.description: When Python raises a ResourceWarning (e.g., for unclosed sockets or file handles), the existing warning output did not include information about where the offending resource was originally allocated, making it difficult to debug. This change enhances the warning_record_to_str function so that, when tracemalloc is active, the allocation traceback of the source object is appended to the warning message. When tracemalloc is available but not active, a helpful hint directing users to enable it (with a link to documentation) is shown instead. This gives users actionable debugging information for ResourceWarning and similar warnings that carry a source object.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that when pytest captures a warning whose WarningMessage has a non-None source attribute, the warning output is enriched with allocation-site information. Specifically: (1) if tracemalloc is active and can provide a traceback for the source object, append that traceback to the warning string; (2) if tracemalloc is available but inactive (no traceback returned), append a guidance message telling the user to enable tracemalloc, along with a link to the relevant documentation page; (3) if tracemalloc is not importable, do not alter the warning string. This primarily aids debugging of ResourceWarning from unclosed resources such as sockets and file handles.

expectation.grounded: The warning_record_to_str function must check warning_message.source for non-None values. When tracemalloc is importable and tracemalloc.get_object_traceback returns a non-None traceback for that source, the formatted traceback must be appended to the warning string under an 'Object allocated at:' heading separated by a leading newline. When tracemalloc is importable but get_object_traceback returns None (tracemalloc inactive), the function must append a message advising the user to enable tracemalloc and include the stable documentation URL for resource-warnings. When tracemalloc cannot be imported, the warning string must remain unchanged. The function must return the (possibly enriched) warning string.
expectation.conceptual: When pytest displays a warning that carries a source object reference, the output should include the allocation traceback of that object if tracemalloc tracing is enabled. If tracing is not enabled but could be, the output should include a user-friendly hint explaining how to enable it. If tracemalloc is entirely unavailable, the warning output should remain as before. The goal is to give users enough information to identify where an unclosed resource was originally created.

constraints.grounded: The tracemalloc import must be guarded so that ImportError does not propagate. The enrichment logic must only activate when warning_message.source is not None, not solely based on the warning category. Existing warning output for warnings without a source attribute must remain completely unchanged. The traceback formatting must use the traceback object's own format method rather than custom formatting.
constraints.conceptual: The feature must degrade gracefully: it must not crash or alter behavior when tracemalloc is unavailable or inactive. Warnings that do not carry a source object must not be affected. The additional output must be clearly separated from the original warning text so it does not confuse existing warning parsers or user expectations.

behavior: When a warning with a non-None source is processed and tracemalloc is active with a recorded traceback for that source, the warning string gains a new section headed 'Object allocated at:' containing the formatted allocation traceback, preceded by a blank line for visual separation.

When a warning with a non-None source is processed and tracemalloc is importable but has no recorded traceback (not started), the warning string gains a hint message advising the user to enable tracemalloc and providing a documentation URL, without a leading blank line.
When a warning with a non-None source is processed but tracemalloc cannot be imported, the warning string is returned unmodified.
When a warning has a None source attribute, regardless of tracemalloc state, the warning string is returned unmodified.
The tracemalloc import is performed lazily inside the function and any ImportError is silently suppressed.
acceptance_criteria: When tracemalloc is active and a ResourceWarning with a non-None source is captured, the warning output contains 'Object allocated at:' followed by the allocation traceback lines.

When tracemalloc is importable but not started and a warning with a non-None source is captured, the warning output contains guidance text mentioning 'Enable tracemalloc' and includes a documentation URL.
When tracemalloc is not importable and a warning with a non-None source is captured, the warning output is identical to the baseline format without any additional text.
When any warning has a None source attribute, the warning output is identical to the baseline format regardless of tracemalloc state.
The allocation traceback section is visually separated from the preceding warning text by a leading newline when a traceback is present.
The hint message (when tracemalloc is inactive) does not include a leading blank line, distinguishing it from the traceback case.
No ImportError or other exception propagates from the tracemalloc integration to the caller of warning_record_to_str.

task_7.title: Expand accepted types in parametrize ids argument
task_7.description: Previously, the `ids` argument to `@pytest.mark.parametrize` and `@pytest.fixture` only accepted `str`, `float`, `int`, and `bool` values. A separate internal code path for auto-generated IDs already supported additional types such as `bytes`, `complex`, `re.Pattern`, `Enum`, and objects with a `__name__` attribute. This change unifies both code paths by introducing a consolidated `IdMaker` class, so that explicitly provided `ids` values now accept the same broad set of types as auto-generated IDs. The type signature of the `ids` parameter is widened from `Union[None, str, float, int, bool]` to `Optional[object]`, with runtime validation for supported types.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the `ids` argument to `@pytest.mark.parametrize` and `@pytest.fixture` accepts `bytes`, `complex`, `re.Pattern`, `Enum`, and any object with a `__name__` attribute, in addition to the previously supported `str`, `float`, `int`, and `bool` types. Previously, passing these additional types as explicit `ids` values would raise an error, even though the same types were already supported when pytest auto-generated IDs from parameter values.

expectation.grounded: The `ids` parameter of `Metafunc.parametrize()`, `@pytest.fixture`, and `FixtureDef` accepts `Optional[object]` values instead of the previous `Union[None, str, float, int, bool]`. The new `IdMaker` class handles ID resolution uniformly. `IdMaker._idval_from_value` returns string representations for `str`, `bytes`, `int`, `float`, `bool`, `complex`, `re.Pattern`, `enum.Enum`, and objects with a `__name__` attribute. `IdMaker._idval_from_value_required` raises a failure with a descriptive message listing all supported types when an unsupported type is provided in explicit `ids`. The `_validate_ids` method no longer performs type-based filtering or coercion — it passes values through directly for later resolution by `IdMaker`.
expectation.conceptual: When a user supplies explicit `ids` values to `@pytest.mark.parametrize` or `@pytest.fixture`, any type that pytest can auto-generate an ID from should also be accepted as an explicit ID. The ID generation for explicit IDs and auto-generated IDs should follow consistent rules. Unsupported types should produce a clear error message enumerating all accepted types.

constraints.grounded: The previously supported types (`str`, `float`, `int`, `bool`, `None`) must continue to work unchanged in the `ids` argument. The `pytest_make_parametrize_id` hook must still be invoked during ID resolution for auto-generated IDs. The `NOTSET` sentinel enum value must not be treated as a regular `Enum` for ID generation purposes — it must fall through to the default. Duplicate ID disambiguation via numeric suffixes must be preserved. The `idfn` callable form of `ids` must remain supported and its error handling must be preserved.
constraints.conceptual: All existing parametrize ID behavior must remain intact. The change must be purely additive — no previously valid `ids` usage should break. Error messages for unsupported types must clearly communicate which types are accepted. The hook-based ID customization mechanism must continue to function.

behavior: Passing a `bytes` value in the `ids` list to `@pytest.mark.parametrize` produces an ASCII-escaped string ID instead of raising a type error.
Passing a `complex` value in the `ids` list produces its `str()` representation as the test ID.
Passing a `re.Pattern` value in the `ids` list produces an ASCII-escaped version of the pattern string as the test ID.
Passing an `enum.Enum` member in the `ids` list produces its `str()` representation as the test ID.
Passing an object with a `__name__` attribute (e.g., a class or function) in the `ids` list uses that `__name__` as the test ID.
Passing an unsupported type in explicit `ids` raises a failure message listing all supported types: str, bytes, int, float, complex, bool, enum, regex, or anything with a __name__.

When an `idfn` callable returns a value of a newly supported type (e.g., `bytes`, `Enum`), that value is now correctly converted to a string ID via the unified code path instead of falling through to argname-based fallback.
The `ids` parameter type annotation in `@pytest.fixture` and `FixtureDef` is widened to accept `Optional[object]` values, matching the broadened runtime acceptance.
acceptance_criteria: When `@pytest.mark.parametrize('x', [1, 2], ids=[b'byte1', b'byte2'])` is used, the test IDs should include the ASCII-escaped byte string representations without raising an error.
When `@pytest.mark.parametrize('x', [1, 2], ids=[1+2j, 3+4j])` is used, the test IDs should be the string representations of the complex numbers.
When `@pytest.mark.parametrize('x', [1, 2], ids=[re.compile('foo'), re.compile('bar')])` is used, the test IDs should be the ASCII-escaped regex pattern strings.
When `@pytest.mark.parametrize('x', [1, 2], ids=[MyEnum.A, MyEnum.B])` is used where `MyEnum` is an `enum.Enum`, the test IDs should be the string representations of the enum members.
When `@pytest.mark.parametrize('x', [1, 2], ids=[int, str])` is used, the test IDs should be 'int' and 'str' (derived from `__name__`).
When `@pytest.mark.parametrize('x', [1], ids=[object()])` is used with an unsupported type, a clear error message should be raised listing all supported types.
When `@pytest.mark.parametrize('x', [1, 2], ids=[True, 3.14])` is used (previously supported types), it should continue to work identically to before.
When duplicate IDs result from explicit `ids` values, numeric suffixes should be appended to disambiguate them (e.g., 'foo0', 'foo1').
When an `idfn` callable is provided and returns a `bytes` or `Enum` value, that value should be properly converted to a string ID.

task_8.title: pytest.approx() raises TypeError for unordered sequences
task_8.description: Previously, pytest.approx() accepted unordered collections such as sets and custom classes implementing only __iter__ and __len__. Because approx relies on positional comparison via zip, unordered inputs could silently yield incorrect results—two equal sets could compare as not-approximately-equal due to non-deterministic iteration order. The fix tightens sequence detection to require ordered access (__getitem__) and explicitly raises a TypeError when an unordered Collection is passed, preventing silent miscomparisons.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that pytest.approx() rejects unordered collections (e.g., sets) with a clear TypeError instead of silently producing incorrect approximate comparison results. Previously, passing a set to pytest.approx() could cause equal sets to compare as unequal because the element-wise comparison relied on iteration order, which is undefined for sets. Additionally, custom classes that only implement __iter__ and __len__ (without __getitem__) should no longer be accepted as sequence-like inputs, since they do not guarantee order.

expectation.grounded: When pytest.approx() receives an expected value that is a Collection (from collections.abc) but does not support __getitem__, it must raise a TypeError. The sequence-like detection in the approx() factory function must check for __getitem__ and Sized rather than Iterable and Sized. The ApproxSequenceLike class __repr__ must no longer include set in its recognized seq_type tuple. Dictionary (Mapping) comparison and ordered sequences (tuple, list, numpy arrays) must continue to work as before.
expectation.conceptual: When a user passes an unordered collection such as a set to pytest.approx(), the library must raise a TypeError with a descriptive message indicating that only ordered sequences are supported. All previously supported ordered types (tuples, lists, numpy arrays) and dictionary mappings must continue to function correctly with approximate comparison.

constraints.grounded: Passing a tuple, list, or numpy array to pytest.approx() must not raise TypeError and must continue element-wise approximate comparison. Passing a Mapping (dict) must continue to use key-based approximate comparison via ApproxMapping. Passing a scalar numeric value must continue to use ApproxScalar. String types must remain excluded from sequence-like handling. The TypeError must be raised before any comparison occurs, at the point where the ApproxBase subclass is selected.
constraints.conceptual: The change must not break any existing behavior for ordered sequences or dictionary comparisons. Only unordered collections are newly rejected. The rejection must happen eagerly when approx() is called, not lazily during comparison, so users get immediate feedback.

behavior: pytest.approx() raises TypeError when the expected value is a set
pytest.approx() raises TypeError when the expected value is a frozenset or any other unordered Collection
pytest.approx() raises TypeError for custom classes implementing __iter__ and __len__ but not __getitem__, since they cannot guarantee order
pytest.approx() continues to accept tuples, lists, and other ordered sequences that implement __getitem__ and Sized
pytest.approx() continues to accept Mapping types (e.g., dict) for key-based approximate comparison
pytest.approx() continues to accept scalar numeric values
The repr of ApproxSequenceLike no longer formats output as a set type; unrecognized sequence types default to list formatting
The docstring for approx() explicitly states that only ordered sequences are supported and that sets are not supported
acceptance_criteria: When pytest.approx() is called with a set (e.g., pytest.approx({1.0, 2.0})), it should raise a TypeError
When pytest.approx() is called with a frozenset, it should raise a TypeError
When pytest.approx() is called with a custom class that implements __iter__ and __len__ but not __getitem__, it should raise a TypeError
When pytest.approx() is called with a list (e.g., pytest.approx([0.1, 0.2])), it should return an ApproxSequenceLike instance and comparison should work correctly
When pytest.approx() is called with a tuple (e.g., pytest.approx((0.1, 0.2))), it should return an ApproxSequenceLike instance and comparison should work correctly
When pytest.approx() is called with a dict (e.g., pytest.approx({'a': 0.1})), it should return an ApproxMapping instance and comparison should work correctly
When pytest.approx() is called with a plain number, it should return an ApproxScalar instance as before
The TypeError message should indicate that only ordered sequences are supported and include a representation of the offending input

task_9.title: Revert deprecation of unittest.SkipTest during collection
task_9.description: The deprecation warning that was emitted when raising unittest.SkipTest to skip tests during pytest's collection phase has been removed. Raising unittest.SkipTest during collection is now a fully supported feature again, restoring the behavior that existed before the deprecation was introduced. Users who relied on unittest.SkipTest at module level to skip entire test modules during collection will no longer see PytestRemovedIn8Warning deprecation warnings.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that raising unittest.SkipTest during the pytest collection phase is a supported feature and does not emit any deprecation warning. Previously, this usage triggered a PytestRemovedIn8Warning advising users to switch to pytest.skip(), but this deprecation has been reverted because unittest.SkipTest during collection is a legitimate use case that should remain supported.

expectation.grounded: When unittest.SkipTest is raised during the collection phase (e.g., at module level in a test file), the collector should produce a CollectReport with outcome 'skipped' without emitting any PytestRemovedIn8Warning or PytestDeprecationWarning. The UNITTEST_SKIP_DURING_COLLECTION warning constant should no longer exist in the deprecated module. The pytest_make_collect_report hook should handle unittest.SkipTest identically to pytest.skip exceptions—producing a skipped outcome with an appropriate ExceptionChainRepr—without any special-case warning branch for unittest.SkipTest.
expectation.conceptual: Raising unittest.SkipTest during test collection should silently skip the collection of the affected module or item, producing a normal 'skipped' result. No deprecation warning should be issued for this usage pattern. The behavior should be indistinguishable from using pytest.skip() during collection in terms of the skip outcome.

constraints.grounded: The existing skip-during-collection behavior must be preserved: when unittest.SkipTest is raised during collection, the CollectReport must still have outcome 'skipped' with a proper ExceptionChainRepr representation. No new warnings or errors should be introduced for this code path. Other deprecation warnings in the deprecated module (e.g., PRIVATE, ARGUMENT_PERCENT_DEFAULT) must remain unaffected. The collection of unittest.SkipTest into skip_exceptions in pytest_make_collect_report must remain intact so the exception is still recognized as a skip signal.
constraints.conceptual: The skip-during-collection mechanism must continue to work correctly for all recognized skip exception types. Removing the deprecation warning must not alter the outcome or reporting of skipped collections. Other existing deprecation warnings in the framework must not be affected by this change.

behavior: Raising unittest.SkipTest at module level or during the collection phase no longer emits a PytestRemovedIn8Warning deprecation warning.
The UNITTEST_SKIP_DURING_COLLECTION deprecation constant is removed from the deprecated module.
When unittest.SkipTest is raised during collection, the resulting CollectReport still has outcome 'skipped' with a proper failure representation.
The collection-phase skip handling no longer has a special-case branch distinguishing unittest.SkipTest from other skip exceptions for warning purposes.
All other skip exceptions (e.g., pytest.skip via Skipped) continue to be handled identically during collection.
acceptance_criteria: When a test module raises unittest.SkipTest at the module level during collection, the module should be reported as 'skipped' with no warnings emitted.

When running pytest with -W error::pytest.PytestRemovedIn8Warning and a test module raises unittest.SkipTest during collection, the collection should succeed with a skip outcome rather than failing due to a deprecation warning being treated as an error.
When collecting a module that raises unittest.SkipTest, the skip reason from the SkipTest exception should appear in the collection report's longrepr.
When collecting a module that raises pytest.skip(), the behavior and outcome should be identical to raising unittest.SkipTest—both should produce a skipped CollectReport with no deprecation warnings.
Given a test suite where no unittest.SkipTest is raised during collection, the collection behavior and output should be completely unchanged from previous versions.

task_11.title: Fix selected test count in terminal collection summary when errors or skipped modules exist
task_11.description: The terminal collection summary incorrectly calculated the number of selected tests when collection errors or skipped modules were present. Errors and skipped modules were subtracted from the selected count even though they did not contribute to the collected item count, resulting in an artificially reduced 'selected' number displayed to the user. The fix ensures only genuinely deselected items (via -k or -m filters) reduce the selected count, and also adjusts the display condition so the selected count is shown whenever it differs from the collected total.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the terminal collection summary displays the correct number of selected tests when there are collection errors or skipped modules. Previously, if a test module failed to import (causing a collection error) or was skipped during collection, the 'selected' count shown in the summary line was incorrectly reduced by the number of errors and skipped modules, even though those modules never contributed items to the collected count. For example, with 3 collected items, 1 deselected, and 1 collection error, the summary would show '1 selected' instead of the correct '2 selected'.

expectation.grounded: The TerminalReporter's collection summary must compute the selected count as the number of collected items minus the number of deselected items only. Errors and skipped module counts must not be subtracted from the selected count. The 'selected' portion of the summary line must be displayed whenever the selected count differs from the collected count (i.e., when _numcollected > selected), without requiring selected > 0.
expectation.conceptual: The selected test count in the collection summary line should accurately reflect how many of the successfully collected tests remain after deselection filters are applied. Collection-phase errors and skipped modules should have no effect on the selected count, since they never contributed collected items. The selected count should be displayed whenever it is less than the total collected count.

constraints.grounded: When no errors or skipped modules are present, the selected count must produce the same result as before (since errors and skipped would be zero). The summary line format ('collected N items / X errors / Y deselected / Z selected') must remain unchanged. The display of error counts and skipped counts in the summary line must not be affected. The selected count must never go negative.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must not alter the display or counting of any other summary statistics (errors, skipped, deselected). The summary line format and other terminal reporter behaviors must remain unchanged. Normal runs without collection errors or skipped modules must be unaffected.

behavior: The selected count is now computed as collected_items minus deselected_items, without subtracting errors or skipped modules.
When collection errors occur, the selected count remains correct and is not reduced by the number of errors.
When modules are skipped during collection, the selected count remains correct and is not reduced by the number of skipped modules.
The 'selected' portion of the summary line is displayed whenever the selected count is less than the total collected count, even if selected is zero.
Previously, the selected portion was only shown when selected > 0, meaning if all items were deselected and errors existed, the selected count could be hidden entirely.
acceptance_criteria: When there are 3 collected items, 1 deselected, and 1 collection error, the summary should show '2 selected' (not '1 selected').
When there are 3 collected items, 1 deselected, and 1 skipped module, the summary should show '2 selected' (not '1 selected').
When there are 3 collected items, 1 deselected, 1 error, and 1 skipped module, the summary should show '2 selected' (not '0 selected' or a missing selected count).
When there are no errors and no skipped modules, the selected count should equal collected minus deselected, same as before.
When all items are deselected (selected = 0) and errors exist, the summary should still display '0 selected' rather than hiding the selected count.
When no items are deselected and no errors/skips exist, the 'selected' portion should not appear in the summary line.

task_12.title: Fix importlib mode package discovery regression when conftest.py exists with PYTHONPATH
task_12.description: Fixed a regression introduced in 7.0.0 where using --import-mode=importlib together with PYTHONPATH or the pythonpath configuration option would cause ModuleNotFoundError when importing from test packages. The root cause was that the insert_missing_modules function unconditionally created dummy module objects for intermediate package names, which prevented the real packages from being importable. The presence of a conftest.py in a test package directory triggered this code path, causing the package to be replaced by a dummy module and breaking cross-module imports within the test suite. The fix attempts to import the real module first before falling back to creating a dummy module placeholder.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that when pytest is configured with --import-mode=importlib and PYTHONPATH (or the pythonpath config option) includes paths that make test directories importable as packages, test modules can successfully import sibling or sub-package modules even when conftest.py files exist in those directories. Previously, the mere existence of a conftest.py in a test package directory caused ModuleNotFoundError for cross-package imports like 'import tests.subpath.helper', because intermediate package modules were replaced with empty placeholders instead of the real packages.

expectation.grounded: The insert_missing_modules function in the pathlib module must attempt to import a real module via importlib.import_module before falling back to creating a dummy ModuleType placeholder. When sys.meta_path is empty, it should skip the import attempt and raise ModuleNotFoundError directly to avoid import warnings. When a real module can be imported (e.g., because pythonpath makes it discoverable), it must be used instead of a dummy module. Only when import_module raises ModuleNotFoundError should a dummy module be registered in sys.modules.
expectation.conceptual: When pytest discovers and collects test files using importlib import mode, it must not interfere with the normal Python import mechanism for packages that are legitimately importable via PYTHONPATH. Intermediate package modules that exist on the Python path should be properly imported rather than replaced with empty stubs. The presence of conftest.py files within a package directory must not disrupt the package's importability.

constraints.grounded: Existing behavior for modules that genuinely do not exist on sys.path must be preserved: dummy ModuleType placeholders must still be created for those modules. The fix must not emit import warnings when sys.meta_path is empty. The fallback to dummy module creation must remain intact for cases where importlib.import_module raises ModuleNotFoundError.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must not break test suites that rely on pytest's existing behavior of creating placeholder modules for packages not on the Python path. The import resolution change should be transparent to users and only affects the order in which modules are resolved, preferring real imports over synthetic placeholders.

behavior: When insert_missing_modules encounters a module name not yet in the modules dict, it first attempts to import it via importlib.import_module instead of immediately creating a dummy module.
If sys.meta_path is empty, the real import attempt is skipped and a ModuleNotFoundError is raised directly to avoid triggering import warnings.
If importlib.import_module succeeds (the module is genuinely importable), the real module is used and no dummy placeholder is created.
If importlib.import_module raises ModuleNotFoundError, the original behavior of creating a dummy ModuleType placeholder is preserved as a fallback.
Test packages that are importable via PYTHONPATH or the pythonpath config option are no longer shadowed by dummy modules during conftest.py collection.
Cross-module imports within test packages (e.g., 'import tests.subpath.helper') now succeed when conftest.py exists in the package directory, matching pre-7.0.0 behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Given a project with --import-mode=importlib and pythonpath=. configured, when a conftest.py exists in the tests/ directory and a test module imports tests.subpath.helper, then the import should succeed without ModuleNotFoundError.

Given a project with --import-mode=importlib and PYTHONPATH set to include the project root, when test packages contain __init__.py files and conftest.py files, then pytest collection should complete without import errors.
When conftest.py is absent from the test package directory, the behavior should remain identical to prior versions with no regressions.
When a module genuinely does not exist on sys.path, insert_missing_modules should still create a dummy ModuleType placeholder as before.
When sys.meta_path is empty, no import warnings should be emitted during the module resolution process.
Given a test suite that previously worked with pytest < 7.0.0 using importlib mode and pythonpath, upgrading to the fixed version should restore the previously working import behavior.

task_10.title: Stop resolving symlinks in conftest paths so symlinked conftests load independently
task_10.description: Previously, pytest resolved symbolic links when identifying conftest.py files, which meant a conftest accessed both directly and through a symlink was treated as the same module and only loaded once. This was inconsistent with how test collection itself handled symlinks since pytest 6.0. The fix removes symlink resolution from conftest path identification, so each distinct path (including symlinked paths) is treated as a separate conftest and loaded independently. A new helper method centralizes the confcutdir boundary check, and the internal conftest deduplication mechanism is replaced with the plugin registry lookup using unresolved paths.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that symbolic link components in conftest.py paths are no longer resolved during conftest discovery and loading. When a conftest.py file appears at multiple locations in the collection tree due to symlinks, each distinct path should result in a separate conftest load and execution. This aligns conftest handling with the symlink-aware test collection behavior introduced in pytest 6.0. Ensure that the confcutdir boundary is consistently applied using a single unified check across conftest discovery and package collection.

expectation.grounded: PytestPluginManager._importconftest should identify conftest modules by their unresolved path string (via get_plugin) rather than by a symlink-resolved Path key. The removed _conftestpath2mod dictionary should no longer be used for conftest deduplication. PytestPluginManager._getconftestmodules should return Sequence[types.ModuleType] instead of List[types.ModuleType]. A new PytestPluginManager._is_in_confcutdir method should encapsulate confcutdir boundary checking and be used in both _getconftestmodules and Session's package discovery. When two paths reference the same physical conftest.py through a symlink, both should be loaded as separate plugin registrations and both should execute their module-level code.
expectation.conceptual: Conftest files should be identified and deduplicated by their apparent filesystem path, not by their resolved real path. If the same conftest.py is reachable via two different paths (one direct, one through a symlink), pytest should treat them as two independent conftests and execute each one. The confcutdir boundary logic should be consistently applied through a single check point across all conftest discovery and collection paths.

constraints.grounded: Conftest modules that are not reached via symlinks must continue to load exactly once. The confcutdir boundary must remain functional: conftests outside the confcutdir must not be loaded. The _dirpath2confmods cache must continue to correctly associate directories with their applicable conftest modules. The plugin registration via register/get_plugin must serve as the deduplication mechanism, keyed by the unresolved string path. The _noconftest flag must still suppress all conftest loading when set.
constraints.conceptual: Non-symlinked conftest behavior must remain unchanged — conftests are loaded once per unique path. The confcutdir boundary must continue to prevent conftest loading above the configured cutoff directory. Conftest loading suppression via the noconftest option must still work. The change must not introduce double-loading of conftests in non-symlink scenarios.

behavior: When a directory tree contains a symlink to another directory that has a conftest.py, running pytest on a parent that covers both the real and symlinked paths will import and execute the conftest twice — once for each path.
Conftest deduplication is now based on the unresolved string path registered in the plugin manager, not on a resolved Path object in a separate dictionary.
The _conftestpath2mod dictionary is removed; conftest lookup uses PytestPluginManager.get_plugin(str(conftestpath)) instead.
A new _is_in_confcutdir method returns True if confcutdir is None or if the given path is within confcutdir, and False otherwise.
The confcutdir parent-checking logic in _getconftestmodules and Session package discovery is replaced by calls to _is_in_confcutdir.
The return type of _getconftestmodules is narrowed from List to Sequence.
The contextlib import is removed as contextlib.suppress is no longer used in conftest loading.
acceptance_criteria: Given a test directory structure with tests/real/conftest.py and tests/link symlinked to tests/real, when running pytest tests, then conftest.py should be imported and executed twice: once as tests/real/conftest.py and once as tests/link/conftest.py.
Given a conftest.py at a single non-symlinked path, when running pytest, then the conftest should be loaded exactly once, preserving existing behavior.
Given a confcutdir set to a specific directory, when conftest discovery encounters paths above that directory, then those conftests should not be loaded regardless of symlinks.
When _noconftest is True, then no conftest modules should be loaded at all, even if symlinked conftest paths exist.
When _importconftest is called with a conftest path that has already been registered as a plugin (by its unresolved string path), then it should return the existing module without re-importing.
When a conftest is newly loaded and its parent directory already exists in _dirpath2confmods, then the module should be appended to all applicable directory entries in that cache.

task_13.title: pytester fixture uses monkeypatch fixture instead of internal MonkeyPatch instance
task_13.description: The pytester fixture previously created its own internal MonkeyPatch instance and manually called undo() during finalization. This caused environment variable teardown ordering issues when a test used both the monkeypatch fixture and pytester together. Environment variables set via monkeypatch (e.g., PY_COLORS) could leak past their expected teardown boundary, remaining visible during session-scoped fixture teardown. The fix changes pytester to request the monkeypatch fixture as a dependency, ensuring that all environment variable modifications follow pytest's standard fixture finalization ordering.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that when a test requests both the `monkeypatch` fixture and the `pytester` fixture, environment variable changes made by `monkeypatch` are fully undone before higher-scoped fixtures (e.g., session-scoped fixtures) run their teardown. Previously, `pytester` created its own internal `MonkeyPatch` instance with independent teardown timing, which caused environment variables set via `monkeypatch.setenv()` to leak into the environment during session-scoped fixture finalization.

expectation.grounded: The `pytester` fixture must accept a `monkeypatch: MonkeyPatch` parameter as a fixture dependency and pass it to the `Pytester` constructor. The `Pytester.__init__` method must accept this `MonkeyPatch` instance instead of instantiating its own. The `Pytester` finalization logic must no longer call `MonkeyPatch.undo()` directly, as the `monkeypatch` fixture's own teardown handles cleanup. Environment variables set by `pytester` via `MonkeyPatch` (such as `PYTEST_DEBUG_TEMPROOT`, `TOX_ENV_DIR`, and color-related variables like `PY_COLORS`, `NO_COLOR`, `FORCE_COLOR`) are cleaned up through the standard `monkeypatch` fixture finalization lifecycle.
expectation.conceptual: The pytester fixture should delegate all environment variable management to the standard monkeypatch fixture rather than managing its own independent MonkeyPatch lifecycle. This ensures that all environment variable mutations introduced by pytester or by the user's test via monkeypatch are undone in the correct fixture teardown order, preventing environment pollution across fixture scopes.

constraints.grounded: Existing tests that use the `pytester` fixture must continue to work without modification. The `Pytester` class must still set `PYTEST_DEBUG_TEMPROOT`, delete `TOX_ENV_DIR`, and manage color-related environment variables (`PY_COLORS`, `NO_COLOR`, `FORCE_COLOR`) via the monkeypatch instance. The `pytester` fixture must not create a standalone `MonkeyPatch()` instance. Session-scoped fixtures must observe a clean environment (no leaked variables) during their teardown when a function-scoped test used both `monkeypatch` and `pytester`.
constraints.conceptual: The change must not break any existing pytester-based test. Environment variable isolation guarantees must be preserved. No environment variable set during a function-scoped test should leak into session-scoped or higher-scoped fixture teardown phases.

behavior: The pytester fixture now declares monkeypatch as a fixture dependency, so pytest resolves and injects it automatically.
The Pytester class uses the injected monkeypatch instance for all environment variable modifications instead of creating a new MonkeyPatch internally.
The Pytester finalization no longer calls MonkeyPatch.undo(), because the monkeypatch fixture handles its own teardown through pytest's fixture lifecycle.
When a test requests both monkeypatch and pytester, all environment variable changes are undone in the correct finalization order dictated by pytest's fixture dependency graph.
Environment variables such as PY_COLORS, NO_COLOR, FORCE_COLOR, PYTEST_DEBUG_TEMPROOT, and TOX_ENV_DIR set by pytester are cleaned up when the monkeypatch fixture finalizes.
Session-scoped fixtures no longer observe leaked environment variables during teardown when function-scoped tests used monkeypatch alongside pytester.
acceptance_criteria: When a test requests both `monkeypatch` and `pytester`, and `monkeypatch.setenv()` sets an environment variable (e.g., PY_COLORS), a session-scoped fixture's teardown should observe that variable as absent from `os.environ`.
When `pytester` is used in a test, environment variables set internally by Pytester (PYTEST_DEBUG_TEMPROOT, TOX_ENV_DIR deletions, color variables) should be fully reverted after the test completes.
When two tests run in sequence where the first uses `pytester` and sets environment variables, the second test should not observe any environment pollution from the first test's pytester usage.
When `pytester` is requested as a fixture, it should not instantiate its own MonkeyPatch; it should use the monkeypatch fixture provided by pytest's fixture system.
When the Pytester instance is finalized, it should not independently call undo() on the MonkeyPatch instance, as cleanup is handled by the monkeypatch fixture's own teardown.

task_14.title: Include file path in malformed pyproject.toml error messages
task_14.description: When pytest encounters a malformed pyproject.toml file during configuration discovery, it previously raised a UsageError containing only the TOML parse error (e.g., line and column numbers) without identifying which file was problematic. This was especially confusing when the malformed file existed in a parent directory, leaving users with no actionable clue. The error message now includes the file path of the offending pyproject.toml alongside the parse error details.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that when pytest encounters a malformed pyproject.toml file during config discovery, the resulting error message identifies the specific file path that failed to parse, so users can locate and fix the problem without manual investigation. This applies regardless of where the malformed file resides in the directory hierarchy (e.g., a parent directory).

expectation.grounded: When load_config_dict_from_file encounters a tomli.TOMLDecodeError while parsing a pyproject.toml, it must raise a UsageError whose message contains both the file path of the malformed pyproject.toml and the original TOML decode error details (line number, column, character information). The original TOMLDecodeError must remain chained as the cause of the UsageError.
expectation.conceptual: When pytest fails to parse a pyproject.toml configuration file, the error message displayed to the user must clearly identify which file could not be parsed, in addition to the TOML syntax error details. Users should be able to determine the exact problematic file from the error output alone, without needing a stack trace or manual debugging.

constraints.grounded: The UsageError must still be raised from the original TOMLDecodeError (preserving the exception chain). The TOML decode error details (line, column, character) must not be lost or truncated from the message. No other error paths or non-TOML config file handling should be affected by this change.
constraints.conceptual: The improvement must not suppress or alter the underlying TOML parse error information. Only the presentation of the error is enhanced. Other configuration file formats and their error handling must remain unchanged.

behavior: When a syntactically invalid pyproject.toml is encountered during config discovery, the raised UsageError message now begins with the file path of the malformed file, followed by the TOML parser's error description.
The error message includes sufficient information (file path, line number, column, offending character) for the user to locate and diagnose the issue directly from the error output.
The exception chain is preserved: the UsageError is raised from the original TOMLDecodeError, maintaining debuggability for users who inspect tracebacks.
Malformed pyproject.toml files in parent directories are now diagnosable from the error message alone, since the full file path is included.
acceptance_criteria: When a malformed pyproject.toml exists in the project directory and pytest is invoked, the error output must contain the file path of the malformed pyproject.toml.
When a malformed pyproject.toml exists in a parent directory and pytest is invoked, the error output must contain the full path to that parent directory's pyproject.toml.
The TOML parse error details (such as line number, column number, and offending character) must still appear in the error message alongside the file path.
The UsageError must preserve the original TOMLDecodeError in its exception chain (raised with 'from' clause).
Valid pyproject.toml files must continue to be parsed and loaded without any change in behavior.
Non-pyproject.toml configuration files (e.g., setup.cfg, pytest.ini) must not be affected by this change.
